<skill-format>true</skill-format>

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.
I'll start by scouting the repo layout, git history, and the live page at 127.0.0.1:18090, then fan out a multi-agent workflow for the deep analysis.

===== README.md =====
# coinpoker-help

Local bug-bounty proof of concept for poker observation and decision support.
Native capture targets Windows 10 version 1903 or later. Structured JSON replay
and poker libraries also run on Linux.
The current helper has no mouse/keyboard input path, client-memory reader, or
client-network interception.

**Status:** engineering candidate, version `0.1.0`; Laya iteration-1 Gate F
**FAIL**, human verification **UNVERIFIED**, no validated live seated advice. A build,
synthetic evaluation or loaded model is not real-table acceptance. Physical
Windows, model, real-image and clean-account evidence is recorded in
[the Windows report](docs/WINDOWS_ACCEPTANCE_V1.md); unrun gates stay `UNRUN`.
Practice and cash use this same repo, representation and validation mechanism,
without a practice-only bypass. No real-money acceptance has been established.

## Start here

- [First manual seated diagnostic: launch, confirm, stop and checklist](docs/SEATED_DIAGNOSTIC.md)
- [Windows setup and local dashboard](docs/INSTALL_WINDOWS.md)
- [VLM compatibility and provenance](docs/VLM_COMPATIBILITY.md)
- [Live JSON-lines contract](docs/EVENTS_V2.md)
- [Visual evaluation contract](docs/VISUAL_EVALUATION_V2.md)
- [Model terms](MODEL_LICENSES.md), [security](SECURITY.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Current model and browser

The sole perception backend is Laya Vision. Reuse the already downloaded and
trained checkpoint `models/laya-vision/finetuned/20261009T190322Z-it1`, based on
`thaitea/laya-vision@f2fe3c12cb6d04c59d8a190250bf3fb40fc828dc` and recorded in
`scripts/laya-pins.json`. No redownload, retraining or new dump is needed for
this dashboard phase. A fresh install lacks this user's local fine-tuned weights.

The canonical browser address is **`http://127.0.0.1:18090/`**. Model metadata
is at `/v1/models` under alias `coinpoker-laya-vision`; typed Laya requests use
`/v1/laya/predict` on the same listener. Gemma, ports `18080`/`8080`,
chat-completions and remote VLM opt-in are retired product instructions, not
alternate endpoints or fallbacks.

The browser has exactly two views, **Monitor** and **Reference** in a compact
landscape companion. Monitor shows source/role/freshness, independent readings,
six physical seats and a separate recorder status; history and diagnostics are
collapsible. A genuine current full native observation and matching decision can
display **EXPERIMENTAL** analysis with `quality_approved:false`; partial readouts
cannot supply it. The pinned model's R17 and untrained hero/control limitations
remain, and no live seated capability or quality certification is claimed.
Reference uses a searchable topic list and selected content, with the existing
bundled education and citations unchanged.
It makes no runtime content requests and does not copy the root charts.

Open `http://127.0.0.1:18090/` beside the selected table. **Stop capture** requests
termination of the current source session through the service-bound local
`POST /api/capture/stop`; it does not need a loaded model. There are currently no
HTTP start/mark, seating or betting controls. For development startup, choose
one mode below, not two concurrent servers; inspect the existing 18090 listener
before starting anything. Reuse an already running service.

```powershell
# Dashboard-only startup without loading a model or using the GPU.
pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -DashboardOnly
```

```powershell
# Normal startup is also dashboard-only. No automatic model load or attachment.
pwsh -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1
```

The role display follows explicit current-source evidence: **Observing**,
**Seated** ("Waiting for your turn"), **Your turn**, or **Reading uncertain**.
Observing call cost/pot odds belong to the labelled acting seat, never a fictitious
"your call". Sitting down changes the role, not the stream or accumulated history.
Unknown readings stay unknown; a missing feed is one compact message, not a grid
of unavailable fields. Expiry, heartbeat loss, hidden/resumed tabs and disconnects
clear current readings without renewing their leases. Runtime/lease/ledger details
and synthetic fixtures stay behind the scenes, not in extra app views.

Normal startup no longer follows a saved selector. `-LiveConfig`, a supplied
`-PracticeConfig` without explicit automatic inference, and server `--auto-attach` are refused. A fresh manual
session requires the fresh exact PID/HWND/nonce challenge via
`scripts/laya_capture.py`, with identity rechecked within 30 seconds. No seating
assertion is required; replacement requires new source confirmation. Default first-session
limits are **600 seconds or 1,200 saved frames**, whichever comes first. Model
loading requires separately approved `-EnableInference`; it never starts capture.
See the [manual runbook](docs/SEATED_DIAGNOSTIC.md) for commands and draft markers.

For explicitly approved observation of one confirmed table window until it closes,
use the sustained mode after verifying/stopping only the owned existing service:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/start-vlm.ps1 -EnableInference -AutomaticInference -ContinuousObservation
```

All three flags are required. This reuses the confirmed private source profile;
it never follows a replacement or changes the poker client. Evidence recording
still stops at 600 seconds, 1,200 saved frames, or 1 GiB, but newly acquired live
frames continue through bounded in-memory transport. Monitor labels that distinction
and puts stop reasons in its main view. Field confidence floors and five-second
reading leases are unchanged; unknown role/activity does not hide independent
admitted numeric fields. Page refresh starts nothing. Source/visibility/owner/model
failure or an explicit stop ends observation without automatic resume. This mode
does not run experimental p6/p7 diagnostics, strategy, or timer recognition.
Synthetic sustained tests are not real-window recognition acceptance.

Some client windows draw the CoinPoker logo and `NLH` number inside their frame
but expose only `CoinPoker` as the OS title. A confirmed private selector can
use that exact OS title. This is **not** an automatic lobby fallback: it requires
explicit user confirmation and still fails on multiple visible matches. Source
identity, current dimensions and perception-quality gates stay independent;
transition/loading/lobby captures are not positive table labels.

Current profile metadata uses `user_scope:"six-max-table"`, not a practice/cash
mode restriction. Legacy `practice-six-max` profiles load with the identical
exact selector, without rewriting the source file or broadening its matches.
`.local/practice-table.json` and `-PracticeConfig` remain compatibility names;
neither names nor window titles prove the actual game mode or layout.

The native recorder saves only private PNGs and a durable SHA-256 manifest under
`.local/captures/<UTC>-practice/`. The historical generic recorder defaults were
7,200 frames, 1 GiB and 500 ms; the new bounded manual entry point overrides the
frame limit to 1,200 and adds the independent 600-second stop.
Caps or I/O failures preserve the prefix and stop new recording without deleting
evidence. The manual session never rearms or follows a replacement. No images, paths or window titles are
served to the browser. Real counters are separate from capture-health counters.
The confirmed real-window B check recorded 900x686 frames, followed the
replacement table and captured its 800x613-to-879x670 resize. SHA-256 audits passed
for 322 original, 9 transition and 118 replacement-prefix frames; old evidence
remains in separate private sessions. This establishes capture and recording,
**not usable recognition**: no observations passed the fitted gate, so Monitor
shows `Reading uncertain`. No timed C/seated session or full reading-to-Monitor
latency acceptance has occurred. Seated controls/hero amounts and calculated metrics
require the later genuine-data/quality checkpoints; a null metric is not zero.
Private session history uses opaque IDs, not player names or cross-session guesses.

Checkpoint A validation: 402 Rust tests passed (one ignored), 79 Python tests
passed, and 47 desktop/400px browser checks passed with no JavaScript errors or
mutation/external requests. Doctor has ten passes and discovery blocked (exit 1).
These tests use synthetic role observations, not real seated recognition or

## Architecture

```text
Windows process and window metadata (exe name, PID, HWND)
  -> unique source-specific confirmed game-window selection, explicit ambiguity
  -> Windows Graphics Capture for the selected window, RGBA frame
  -> cumulative and local pixel change checks, persistently animated tiles
     suppressed (seat avatars, badges, glows), stability gate
  -> one inference worker and one replaceable latest frame
  -> generation, epoch, window identity and capture-age checks
  -> strict screen classification and complete poker-state validation
  -> two matching fresh observations and hand transition guards
  -> Monte Carlo equity and legal decision pipeline
  -> JSON-lines status, leased decision, clear, or discarded event
```

The native capture loop continues during a blocking local Laya
request. A changed or lost window, ambiguous selection, stale frame, or expired
lease clears active advice. Configured source identity and strict recognition,
quality and action validation are required before a visual recommendation. Repeated
model agreement is not independent proof of correct recognition; the held-out
real-image gate remains necessary.

The workspace crates are `ingest` (capture and vision), `core-engine` (poker math),
`ghost-layer` (unwired timing primitives), `opponent-model`, `ui` (unwired native
desktop panel), and `bin` (CLI, replay, diagnostics and evaluation). The current
browser is a local observation dashboard with no input execution layer. Observed
controls, history, calculated metrics and eventual recommendations stay separate;
legacy table events and raw model answers are not trusted current hero actions.

## Structured replay

`--stdin` consumes one complete `GameState` per line and retains its existing bare
decision and clear records. It does not need capture or model setup. Invalid input
clears an active recommendation once; later valid input may recover.

```json
{"game_phase":"flop","hero_cards":[{"rank":"A","suit":"spades"},{"rank":"K","suit":"hearts"}],"board":[{"rank":"A","suit":"diamonds"},{"rank":"7","suit":"clubs"},{"rank":"2","suit":"spades"}],"pot_size":1000,"to_call":500,"hero_chips":5000,"min_raise_to":1500,"max_raise_to":5000,"players":[{"name":"Hero","chips":5000,"last_action":"check","bet_amount":0},{"name":"Villain","chips":4500,"last_action":"bet","bet_amount":500}],"action_required":true,"available_actions":["fold","call","raise"]}
```

## Known limits

- Pixel checks reject malformed, blank and tiny frames; they do not positively
  identify a real table. Wrong title calibration and correlated model errors remain
  possible.
- The 8-second maximum frame age is independent of the tighter 5-second total
  deadline. Published leases use the shorter remaining limit, not a new lifetime
  from delivery. Consumers must honor invalidation, absolute expiry and EOF even
  when capture blocks.
- Persistently animated tiles (seat avatars, badges, glows) are excluded from
  change detection while they animate, so a state change inside such a tile is
  only picked up by the periodic forced refresh (5 s by default), not instantly.
  On a live six-max table real state changes arrive every few hundred
  milliseconds; an inference of several seconds rarely finds a quiet window.
- Strict continuity may suppress valid hands after missed frames or street changes.
  Multiway all-in and side-pot decisions remain suppressed; poker math is unchanged.
- Real image accuracy, end-to-end latency, DPI behavior, window occlusion, restart
  recovery and clean-account packaging require recorded physical evidence.
- Six-max capture support is not complete six-player strategy support. Preserve
  heads-up-only raising and multiway all-in/side-pot guards. Unknown cards,
  amounts, offered actions and history stay unavailable, not fabricated zeros.
- Laya server/dashboard support and the local fine-tuned checkpoint are absent
  from the historical release packaging. The source-free bundle is not a current
  Laya/dashboard installation; this phase makes no release/workflow changes.
- Lobby evaluation is thin: one eval-only image does not validate general lobby
  recognition or the configured lobby-size guard. Capture cursor compositing
  remains a limitation, and currency-glyph handling is untested.
- Weights remain local-only and nonredistributed. Template matching is an option
  for the user's decision, not an implemented or validated substitute for Laya.
- Root `lobby-screengrab.png` remains for the user to delete. The private eval-only
  copy and the reference PNGs/PDF are retained; the helper does not delete them.

===== .kilo plan =====
# Hybrid Rust/Python Architecture Simplification Plan

## 1. Goal & Architectural Findings

Simplify the hybrid Rust/Python codebase by unifying duplicated geometry/region configuration, factoring internal modules in `scripts/laya-server.py`, and consolidating shared session/receipt/test boundaries in `bin/` without changing any external CLI, HTTP API, or test behavior.

### Validated Codebase Boundaries (vs. Initial Assumptions)
1. **Runtime Python Coupling**:
   - `scripts/laya-server.py` imports `laya_dashboard` and `laya_capture` at module load time, and `laya_dashboard.ManualSessionFeed.__init__` (used in `serve` mode) instantiates `laya_visual.VisualWorker`, which transitively imports `laya_board`, `laya_actions`, `laya_showdown`, `laya_numeric`, `laya_context`, `laya_evidence`, and `laya_prep`.
   - Over 20 test modules under `scripts/tests/` import `laya_*.py` directly from `scripts/` and resolve `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`. Therefore, existing top-level module paths in `scripts/` must remain intact.
2. **Supervisor/Child Split (`laya_capture.py` vs. `bin/manual_capture.rs`)**:
   - `scripts/laya_capture.py` (with `laya_attach.py`) is the parent supervisor that confirms windows, writes `.local/laya/manual-capture/<session_id>/approval.json`, manages `active.lock` / `status.json` / `STOP` / `run.json` / `summary.json`, and spawns `coinpoker --capture-only` or `coinpoker --manual-inference` (`bin/manual_capture.rs` and `bin/manual_inference.rs`). Both sides are required.
3. **Existing Hygiene & Manifests**:
   - `.gitignore` already excludes `/.conda/`, `/.local/`, `__pycache__/`, and `*.pyc`.
   - `scripts/vlm-pins.json` is still referenced by `.github/workflows/release-windows.yml` and documented as a retained historical manifest, so it must not be deleted.

---

## 2. Ordered Implementation Tasks

### Phase 1: Unify Geometry & Region Configuration (`regions.json` Single Source of Truth)

**Files**:
- `crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json` (canonical source, read-only)
- `scripts/laya_prep.py`
- `scripts/laya_visual.py`
- `scripts/laya_numeric.py`
- `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs`
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_board.py` (or dedicated geometry parity test in `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py`)

**Steps**:
1. **Centralize `regions.json` loading in `scripts/laya_prep.py`**:
   - Add `REGIONS_REL_PATH = "crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json"` and a stdlib-only helper `load_regions(root=None)` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` that loads and parses `crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json` (using `functools.lru_cache` when `root is None`, and resolving relative to `Path(root)` when a custom root is supplied).
   - Derive `TITLE_BAR_PX`, `TITLE_BAR_RANGE`, and `CONTENT_ASPECT` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` from `load_regions()["geometry"]` (`title_bar_px`, `tuple(title_bar_range_px)`, `content_aspect`) while keeping those module-level constant names exported for backward compatibility.
   - Add `region_px(name, w, h, *, regions=None)` in `scripts/laya_prep.py` mirroring `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs::region_px`.
   - Keep `numpy` and `PIL` imports strictly lazy inside `_text_score`, `_text_mask`, `_components`, and `segment_glyphs` so importing `laya_prep` for geometry remains stdlib-only.
2. **Reuse `laya_prep.load_regions` across Python consumers**:
   - Update `scripts/laya_visual.py` (`VisualWorker._load`) and `scripts/laya_numeric.py` (`NumericReader.__init__`) to call `laya_prep.load_regions(self.root)` instead of duplicating raw `(self.root / "crates/ingest/assets/laya/regions.json").read_bytes()` JSON loads.
3. **Add cross-language Rust/Python geometry parity coverage**:
   - Expand `crates/ingest/src/laya/geometry.rs` tests and Python unit tests to verify identical `(x0, y0, cw, ch)` and `box_px` outputs across all 20 named regions in `regions.json` and across standard, letterboxed, pillarboxed, tiny, and `.5` half-to-even tie dimensions (e.g., dimensions where `w / content_aspect` or `avail_h * content_aspect` lands near `.5`).

---

### Phase 2: Internal Modularization of `scripts/laya-server.py`

**Files**:
- `scripts/laya-server.py`
- `scripts/laya_server_validation.py` (new internal helper module)
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py`

**Constraints & Test Contracts to Preserve**:
- `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py` and `scripts/tests/test_laya_dashboard.py` load `scripts/laya-server.py` via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and access/patch module attributes on `srv`:
  - `srv.ROOT`, `srv.REPO`, `srv.HOST`, `srv.PORT`, `srv.PNG_SIG`, `srv.MAX_BODY`, `srv.MAX_READOUT_QUESTIONS`, `srv.MAX_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT`
  - `srv.ACCEPTANCE_PASSES`, `srv.STACK_PASSES`, `srv.WAGER_PASSES`, `srv.SCENE_PASSES`, `srv.WAGER_NOTE`, `srv.SCENE_NOTE`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_WAGER_NOTE`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_CHECKPOINT`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_MODEL_SHA256`, `srv.EXPERIMENTAL_BOUNDS`, `srv.SCENE_QUESTIONS`
  - `srv.RequestError`, `srv.load_pins`, `srv.png_size`, `srv.validate_request`, `srv.shape_answers`, `srv.answer_diagnostics`, `srv.wager_questions`, `srv.readout_core_template`
  - `srv.load_acceptance_floors`, `srv.load_seat_registry`, `srv.load_wager_registry`, `srv.load_scene_registry`, `srv.pinned_file_entries`, `srv.experimental_descriptor`, `srv.load_experimental_metadata`
  - `srv.Engine`, `srv.Service`, `srv.BoundedHTTPServer`, `srv.make_handler`, `srv.handle_predict`, `srv.handle_predict_batch`, `srv.verify`, `srv.cmd_verify`, `srv.cmd_fetch`, `srv.cmd_serve`, `srv.main`
- `test_invalid_report_precedes_every_heavy_import_and_model_load` intercepts `builtins.__import__` and forbids importing `laya`, `laya_prep`, `torch`, `PIL`, or `numpy` before `load_acceptance_floors(pins)` succeeds inside `Engine.__init__`.
- `AcceptanceTests` and experimental metadata tests patch `srv.ROOT` and `srv.REPO` via `unittest.mock.patch.object(srv, ...)`.

**Steps**:
1. **Extract pure request/protocol validation & diagnostics into `scripts/laya_server_validation.py`**:
   - Move protocol constants (`MAX_*`, `ID_RE`, `LAYOUTS`, `GLYPH_STYLES`, `PNG_SIG`, `ACCEPTANCE_PASSES`, `STACK_PASSES`, `WAGER_PASSES`, `SCENE_PASSES`, `WAGER_NOTE`, `SCENE_NOTE`, `EXPERIMENTAL_*`, `SCENE_QUESTIONS`), `RequestError`, `png_size`, `validate_request`, `shape_answers`, `answer_diagnostics`, `pinned_file_entries`, and `experimental_descriptor` into `scripts/laya_server_validation.py` (stdlib-only, zero heavy imports).
   - For filesystem-bound loaders (`load_acceptance_floors`, `load_seat_registry`, `load_experimental_metadata`, `wager_questions`, `readout_core_template`), accept explicit `root` / `repo` parameters in `laya_server_validation.py` and keep thin wrappers in `scripts/laya-server.py` that pass `srv.ROOT` / `srv.REPO` so `patch.object(srv, "ROOT", ...)` and `patch.object(srv, "REPO", ...)` in `test_laya_server.py` continue to work identically.
2. **Deduplicate `handle_predict` and `handle_predict_batch` decode/glyph-prep helpers**:
   - Extract shared image decode + glyph segmentation + question filtering logic used by both `handle_predict` and `handle_predict_batch` into a single internal helper `_decode_and_prepare_pass(engine, layout, style, raw, questions)` so single and batch prediction paths do not duplicate decode/segmentation error handling.
3. **Re-export all public/tested symbols in `scripts/laya-server.py`**:
   - Import and expose every constant, exception, and helper in `scripts/laya-server.py` so external callers and `test_laya_server.py` / `test_laya_dashboard.py` require zero test modifications.

---

### Phase 3: Factor Shared Rust `bin/` Session Helpers & Inline Test Modules

**Files**:
- `bin/manual_capture.rs`
- `bin/manual_inference.rs`
- `bin/live.rs`
- `bin/manual_capture/tests.rs` (or `#[path = ...]` submodule if extracted)
- `bin/manual_inference/tests.rs`
- `bin/live/tests.rs`

**Steps**:
1. **Consolidate shared manual session receipt & source-matching helpers in `bin/manual_capture.rs`**:
   - Extract a shared helper in `bin/manual_capture.rs` for computing `recording_end_reason` + base `manual_capture` status JSON fields (`elapsed_ms`, `stop_reason`, `recording_end_reason`, `recording`, `capture_failures`, `capture_directory`, `latest_frame`, `updated_at_unix_ms`) used by both `manual_capture::emit_status` and `manual_inference::ManualSource::progress`.
   - Extract a shared single-window discovery matcher (`find_approved_window(windows: &[WindowInfo], approved: &WindowInfo) -> Option<&WindowInfo>`) used by both `manual_capture::capture_loop` and `manual_inference::ManualSource::current_window`.
2. **Split oversized inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` out of `bin/` production files**:
   - `bin/manual_inference.rs` is 3,504 lines (2,500+ lines of tests starting at line 1001), `bin/live.rs` is 2,189 lines (1,277 lines of tests starting at line 912), and `bin/manual_capture.rs` is 808 lines (381 lines of tests starting at line 426).
   - Move the inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks into dedicated test submodule files (`bin/manual_capture_tests.rs`, `bin/manual_inference_tests.rs`, `bin/live_tests.rs` wired via `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "..."] mod tests;`) so the production modules in `bin/` remain under ~1,000 lines and easy to navigate while keeping `super::*` private item visibility and test names 100% identical.

---

## 3. Risks & Failure Modes

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Breaking `patch.object(srv, "ROOT", ...)` or `patch.object(srv, "REPO", ...)` in `scripts/tests/test_laya_server.py` | Unit tests in `AcceptanceTests` and `ExperimentalBetActionTests` fail | Keep `ROOT` and `REPO` in `scripts/laya-server.py` and pass them from wrapper functions into any extracted helper in `laya_server_validation.py`. |
| Triggering heavy imports (`laya_prep`, `numpy`, `PIL`, `torch`) before `load_acceptance_floors` in `Engine.__init__` | `test_invalid_report_precedes_every_heavy_import_and_model_load` fails | Ensure `laya_server_validation.py` is strictly stdlib-only and `laya_prep` remains lazily imported inside `Engine.__init__` after floor validation. |
| Breaking `scripts/validate.py` or release packaging workflows | CI or local validation fails | Keep all existing entrypoint paths (`scripts/laya-server.py`, `scripts/laya_prep.py`, `scripts/vlm-pins.json`, `bin/main.rs`) unchanged. |
| Subtle rounding divergence between Rust `f64::round_ties_even` and Python `round` | Region crops differ by 1px on tie dimensions | Both languages use round-half-to-even (`round()` in Python 3, `f64::round_ties_even()` in Rust); verify with explicit `.5` tie test cases in both test suites. |

---

## 4. Verification Plan

Run the full validation suite in order after implementation:

1. **Rust formatting, compilation, and lints**:
   - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
   - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked`
   - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`
2. **Rust unit & integration tests (all 622+ tests)**:
   - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked`
3. **Python test suite (all `scripts/tests/test_*.py` modules)**:
   - `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v`
4. **Full repository validation runner**:
   - `python scripts/validate.py`

197	## Architecture
198	
199	```text
200	Windows process and window metadata (exe name, PID, HWND)
201	  -> unique source-specific confirmed game-window selection, explicit ambiguity
202	  -> Windows Graphics Capture for the selected window, RGBA frame
203	  -> cumulative and local pixel change checks, persistently animated tiles
204	     suppressed (seat avatars, badges, glows), stability gate
205	  -> one inference worker and one replaceable latest frame
206	  -> generation, epoch, window identity and capture-age checks
207	  -> strict screen classification and complete poker-state validation
208	  -> two matching fresh observations and hand transition guards
209	  -> Monte Carlo equity and legal decision pipeline
210	  -> JSON-lines status, leased decision, clear, or discarded event
211	```

213	The native capture loop continues during a blocking local Laya
214	request. A changed or lost window, ambiguous selection, stale frame, or expired
215	lease clears active advice. Configured source identity and strict recognition,
216	quality and action validation are required before a visual recommendation. Repeated
217	model agreement is not independent proof of correct recognition; the held-out
218	real-image gate remains necessary.

317	## Known limits
318	
319	- Pixel checks reject malformed, blank and tiny frames; they do not positively
320	  identify a real table. Wrong title calibration and correlated model errors remain
321	  possible.
322	- The 8-second maximum frame age is independent of the tighter 5-second total
323	  deadline. Published leases use the shorter remaining limit, not a new lifetime
324	  from delivery. Consumers must honor invalidation, absolute expiry and EOF even
325	  when capture blocks.
326	- Persistently animated tiles (seat avatars, badges, glows) are excluded from
327	  change detection while they animate, so a state change inside such a tile is
328	  only picked up by the periodic forced refresh (5 s by default), not instantly.
329	  On a live six-max table real state changes arrive every few hundred
330	  milliseconds; an inference of several seconds rarely finds a quiet window.
331	- Strict continuity may suppress valid hands after missed frames or street changes.
332	  Multiway all-in and side-pot decisions remain suppressed; poker math is unchanged.
333	- Real image accuracy, end-to-end latency, DPI behavior, window occlusion, restart
334	  recovery and clean-account packaging require recorded physical evidence.
335	- Six-max capture support is not complete six-player strategy support. Preserve
336	  heads-up-only raising and multiway all-in/side-pot guards. Unknown cards,
337	  amounts, offered actions and history stay unavailable, not fabricated zeros.
338	- Laya server/dashboard support and the local fine-tuned checkpoint are absent
339	  from the historical release packaging. The source-free bundle is not a current
340	  Laya/dashboard installation; this phase makes no release/workflow changes.
341	- Lobby evaluation is thin: one eval-only image does not validate general lobby
342	  recognition or the configured lobby-size guard. Capture cursor compositing
343	  remains a limitation, and currency-glyph handling is untested.
344	- Weights remain local-only and nonredistributed. Template matching is an option
345	  for the user's decision, not an implemented or validated substitute for Laya.
346	- Root `lobby-screengrab.png` remains for the user to delete. The private eval-only
347	  copy and the reference PNGs/PDF are retained; the helper does not delete them.

1594	## Architecture and code quality of the hybrid Rust/Python system  grade C+ (62/100)
1595	The hybrid split is sound in principle and clean at the manifest level: the five library crates declare no dependencies on each other and are wired only by `bin`, the Windows-only surface is confined to one `cfg(target_os)` module, and Python owns exactly what Rust should not (torch model serving, dashboard projection, process supervision, CPU recognition). The seams that matter for safety are engineered carefully at every layer: loopback-only transport, fail-closed DTO validation, schema-2 JSONL records whose leases can only shorten, and a 256 KiB publication cap; and the uncommitted refactor is a faithful code-motion step in the right direction (manual_inference.rs 3,504 to 900 lines, live.rs 2,189 to 913, laya-server.py 1,632 to 1,259, Python geometry constants now derived from regions.json). The dominant structural defect is that contracts are carried by repetition rather than by a shared source: the partial-observation field allowlist, the pinned acceptance floors, the DRAFT experimental crop bounds and the readout-batch convention each exist in two to five hand-copied places across Rust, Python and JavaScript, and no test exercises a Rust-built request against the Python validator, so drift passes both suites and fails only live. Geometry is unified only for the twelve trained regions; the actions, context, showdown and numeric lanes keep four incompatible reference systems with different title-bar handling and duplicated helper functions. Roughly 60% of library-crate code is inert on the live path (outs/ranges/table_rules, temporal/profile, the egui panel that the CLI refuses, the observer's action recording that only ever receives quality_approved:false), the core-engine module doc claims an integration that does not exist, and the lockfile carries two rand and two thiserror majors while CI compiles eframe for a feature nothing can launch. The remaining monoliths, a 2,858-line browser IIFE with 52 mutable module variables, a 2,411-line dashboard module with a 562-line ingest method and ~300 unreachable supervisor lines, and a server file with 19 unused imports, are exactly where every new lane must land. The test estate violates the evidence boundary by writing fixtures into .local/laya/train, and the CI definition cannot collect the Python suite on a clean clone because two modules import numpy/PIL at module level and one imports a gitignored file. Two perception pipelines now run side by side (Rust-assembled GPU partial_observation and Python CPU provisional lanes) with differently shaped DTOs merged only in the browser, so the hybrid is drifting toward two systems. The structure can carry the next phase only if the contract and geometry sources are unified first; otherwise each new field or region costs five coordinated edits in three languages.

1700	## Security, privacy and licensing posture  grade C+ (72/100)
1701	The loopback boundary itself is engineered well above proof-of-concept norms and I verified it in code rather than taking the maps on faith: the stdlib server requires exactly one Host in {127.0.0.1:port, localhost:port} and at most one matching Origin, discards POST bodies before answering 403, and stamps every hardened response with a default-src 'none' CSP, no-store, nosniff and no-referrer (scripts/laya-server.py:856-865, 884-895; scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37-38); the Rust client refuses any non-loopback host, credentials, query or fragment, never follows redirects or reads proxy env, bounds every body, and the product layer additionally pins port 18090 and /v1/laya/predict (crates/ingest/src/vlm.rs:146-196; bin/config.rs:311-318); no subprocess uses a shell, the Windows OCR helper takes bounded JSON over stdin, private paths are junction/symlink/reparse-guarded on both the Python and Rust sides, the browser receives an opaque 16-hex source_id rather than pid/hwnd/exe, feed failures are regex-redacted, and no secrets or .env files are tracked. Model licensing is handled correctly where it matters: weights are ignored at two levels, only models/.gitignore is tracked, the CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 derivative is documented as local-only in MODEL_LICENSES.md and scripts/laya-pins.json, pinned artifacts are size+SHA-256 verified, and every direct Rust dependency is MIT/Apache (rs_poker Apache-2.0). The posture loses its grade on fidelity and hygiene, not on the boundary. The shipped DTO contradicts the written policy in three places I traced end to end: OCR-recognised player screen names are published to the browser and rendered in seat cards, and are also persisted to .local/laya/events/<id>/context.jsonl; popup HWND/owner HWND/PID/window_class ride into /api/state via the profile capture when a tooltip is read and app.js explicitly accepts them; and GET /api/evidence/<sha256> serves original capture PNGs, while SECURITY.md, README, EVENTS_V2 and CONTRIBUTING all still promise no names, no native HWND/PID data and no images in browser output. Licensing of tracked content is weaker than the model story: a 16.5 MB PokerNews cheat-sheet PDF and two third-party reference-card PNGs are committed and pushed under an MIT LICENSE with no notice, while the design doc states they are untracked. A public test file hard-codes six real opponents' screen names next to private capture hashes, directly against CONTRIBUTING's rule. Evidence integrity is being eroded by the test suite itself, which writes thousands of synthetic sessions into the real .local evidence tree and imports a gitignored script. Residual loopback risks (SO_REUSEADDR on the listener, control_id published in /api/state, stdlib fallthrough for HEAD/OPTIONS, no dependency audit, version-only pip pins) are real but acknowledged by SECURITY.md's "unauthenticated listener" statement and do not block the stated live-readout goal.

<result>{"reportA":"## Part A. Frontend appraisal: the Monitor at 127.0.0.1:18090

### A.1 What the page is and how it is built

The Monitor is a dependency-free page with two tabs, Monitor and Reference (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:24-27`). The stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` in `scripts/laya-server.py` serves it on loopback. The code is three hand-written files:

- `scripts/dashboard/index.html`: 153 lines.
- `scripts/dashboard/styles.css`: 282 lines.
- `scripts/dashboard/app.js`: 2,858 lines, all in one IIFE.

There is no build step, no package manifest and no lint or type tooling.

How it runs, verified in code:

- **Polling.** It requests `GET /api/state` every 250 ms with one request in flight at most (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:361`). Each request aborts after 1.5 s (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:362`) and is capped at 256 KiB (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:366`). The server answers over HTTP/1.0 with `Connection: close` (`scripts/laya-server.py:860`).
- **Rendering.** All text is written through `textContent`. A 100 ms `setInterval(refreshClocks)` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2856`) expires leases and re-renders the page.
- **Leases.** Every lane holds a wall-clock and a monotonic deadline. A deadline can only get shorter.
- **Mutations.** The only writes are `POST /api/capture/start|stop`, and they need a control id.
- **Reference.** The Reference text is bundled into `scripts/dashboard/app.js:4-359`, so the tab makes no requests.

**Coverage limits.** The audit ran against a dashboard-only server with no model and no capture. Three paths were therefore verified in code only: provisional values, last-read values and Start/Stop while a request is pending. Screenshots are in `C:/Users/cld-main/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cld-main-Desktop-github-projects-coinpoker-help/9a033a56-779b-418e-881d-7f600baf0875/scratchpad/shots/`.

**Lens key:** IA (workflow and information architecture), VIS (visual design), A11Y (accessibility), ENG (front-end engineering), SEC (browser/service boundary), PERF (runtime performance), CON (documented contract and tests).

### A.2 What is genuinely good

- **It fails closed.** Nothing renders as current unless it has a source-bound capture and a lease that can only shorten (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2422-2510`). Zero is kept distinct from unknown (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:479-486`). The defects below either misstate the page's state or hide its cues; none of them shows a false number.
- **The boundary is hardened, and this was verified live.**
  - Strict CSP, nosniff and no-referrer headers (`scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37-38`).
  - Host and Origin allowlists. They rejected a foreign Host, a missing Host, `Origin: null` and a duplicated Host (`scripts/laya-server.py:884-895`).
  - No HTML-string sinks anywhere.
  - Response reads are bounded (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:575-614`).
  - Server data is validated against closed vocabularies and checked against the expected capture scope (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:942-981`).
- **The accessibility foundations are real.**
  - A skip link (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:14`).
  - A roving-tabindex tablist (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2821-2836`).
  - Focus moves into player details and returns from them (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1546`, `1724-1730`).
  - The live region de-duplicates announcements (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:569-573`).
  - Cards are `role="img"` and carry provenance in their names (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:1215-1226`).
  - Text contrast is 7.2:1 or better.
  - A DOM probe showed that the Reference topic buttons do have accessible names.
- **The layout fits the target window.** A subgrid table sits over an isolated SVG (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:69-87`). It fits status, controls, six seats, board and pot at 800x600 with no scrolling (02-clean-load-800x600.jpg). It reflows to two columns at 375 px without horizontal overflow.
- **The visible copy is honest.**
  - "A dash is unknown" (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:122`).
  - The board dims last-seen cards and says so (`scripts/dashboard/styles.css:143`, `scripts/dashboard/app.js:1632`). This is the pattern the seats should copy.
- **It is passive and well tested.**
  - Suspend and resume never start capture (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2643-2661`).
  - 139 Node-driven tests pin the lease semantics (for example `scripts/tests/test_companion_ui.py:1396`, `1771`).
  - The bundled reference is parity-tested (`scripts/tests/test_poker_reference.py:245`).

### A.3 Findings

#### Critical / High

There are no critical findings.

**H1. One failed poll leaves never-read fields labelled "Stale" (effort: small)**

- **Lenses:** IA (high), ENG (high), SEC (medium), CON (medium). PERF's stall finding (M6) is what triggers it.
- **Evidence:**
  - `disconnected()` calls `clearObservation("stale")` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2371-2378`).
  - That function's default parameter is the stored `clearReason` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2358-2359`), so the stale reason is persisted.
  - The `observation: null` path and `resume()` call it with no argument (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2425`, `2658`), which keeps "stale".
  - Only a successful admission resets the reason (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2501`).
  - `reasonFor()` then returns "Stale" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:504-508`), and Diagnostics shows "Reading expired" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2202`).
  - Seen live: 01-first-load-sticky-stale-800x600.jpg shows "Stale" under the pot and "Unknown / Stale" on the board. 02-clean-load-800x600.jpg shows "Insufficient context" instead.
  - Every tab hide and show takes the same path. The existing harness could catch this, but no test does.
- **Impact:** After any timeout or tab switch, the operator is told a reading existed and then expired, when nothing was ever admitted.
- **Fix:**
  - Pass "stale" only when a lease was actually active; the `wasActive` value at `scripts/dashboard/app.js:2360` already holds this.
  - Require an explicit reason at every call.
  - Add a test: a failed poll followed by an idle snapshot must show "Insufficient context".

**H2. Seat validity is shown only by colour and a 7 px dot; "Last read" labels are clipped (effort: small)**

- **Lenses:** IA (high), VIS (high), A11Y (high, plus a low finding on forced colours), CON (HANDOFF wording, low).

1	## Part A. Frontend appraisal: the Monitor at 127.0.0.1:18090
2	
3	### A.1 What the page is and how it is built
4	
5	The Monitor is a dependency-free page with two tabs, Monitor and Reference (`scripts/dashboard/index.html:24-27`). The stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer` in `scripts/laya-server.py` serves it on loopback. The code is three hand-written files:
6	
7	- `scripts/dashboard/index.html`: 153 lines.
8	- `scripts/dashboard/styles.css`: 282 lines.
9	- `scripts/dashboard/app.js`: 2,858 lines, all in one IIFE.
10	
11	There is no build step, no package manifest and no lint or type tooling.
12	
13	How it runs, verified in code:
14	
15	- **Polling.** It requests `GET /api/state` every 250 ms with one request in flight at most (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:361`). Each request aborts after 1.5 s (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:362`) and is capped at 256 KiB (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:366`). The server answers over HTTP/1.0 with `Connection: close` (`scripts/laya-server.py:860`).
16	- **Rendering.** All text is written through `textContent`. A 100 ms `setInterval(refreshClocks)` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2856`) expires leases and re-renders the page.
17	- **Leases.** Every lane holds a wall-clock and a monotonic deadline. A deadline can only get shorter.
18	- **Mutations.** The only writes are `POST /api/capture/start|stop`, and they need a control id.
19	- **Reference.** The Reference text is bundled into `scripts/dashboard/app.js:4-359`, so the tab makes no requests.
20	
21	**Coverage limits.** The audit ran against a dashboard-only server with no model and no capture. Three paths were therefore verified in code only: provisional values, last-read values and Start/Stop while a request is pending. Screenshots are in `C:/Users/cld-main/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cld-main-Desktop-github-projects-coinpoker-help/9a033a56-779b-418e-881d-7f600baf0875/scratchpad/shots/`.
22	
23	**Lens key:** IA (workflow and information architecture), VIS (visual design), A11Y (accessibility), ENG (front-end engineering), SEC (browser/service boundary), PERF (runtime performance), CON (documented contract and tests).
24

Zero is kept distinct from unknown (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:479-486`). The defects below either misstate the page's state or hide its cues; none of them shows a false number.
28	- **The boundary is hardened, and this was verified live.**
29	  - Strict CSP, nosniff and no-referrer headers (`scripts/laya_server_validation.py:37-38`).
30	  - Host and Origin allowlists. They rejected a foreign Host, a missing Host, `Origin: null` and a duplicated Host (`scripts/laya-server.py:884-895`).
31	  - No HTML-string sinks anywhere.

57	**H1. One failed poll leaves never-read fields labelled "Stale" (effort: small)**
58	
59	- **Lenses:** IA (high), ENG (high), SEC (medium), CON (medium). PERF's stall finding (M6) is what triggers it.
60	- **Evidence:**
61	  - `disconnected()` calls `clearObservation("stale")` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2371-2378`).
62	  - That function's default parameter is the stored `clearReason` (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2358-2359`), so the stale reason is persisted.
63	  - The `observation: null` path and `resume()` call it with no argument (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2425`, `2658`), which keeps "stale".
64	  - Only a successful admission resets the reason (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2501`).
65	  - `reasonFor()` then returns "Stale" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:504-508`), and Diagnostics shows "Reading expired" (`scripts/dashboard/app.js:2202`).

67	  - Every tab hide and show takes the same path. The existing harness could catch this, but no test does.
68	- **Impact:** After any timeout or tab switch, the operator is told a reading existed and then expired, when nothing was ever admitted.

70	  - Pass "stale" only when a lease was actually active; the `wasActive` value at `scripts/dashboard/app.js:2360` already holds this.

72	  - Add a test: a failed poll followed by an idle snapshot must show "Insufficient context".

339	### A.5 Recommended refactor shape
340	
341	Keep the zero-dependency, no-build, strict-CSP design. `script-src 'self'` already allows `<script type="module">`, so the change is only splitting the file and adding the new files to the server's asset map.
342	
343	- **Module layout.**
344	  - `constants.js` and `clock.js`. Inject one `{wall(), mono()}` clock instead of 65 scattered clock calls.
345	  - `dto/*.js`. Normalizers return `{value, reason}`, never a bare `null`.
346	  - `lease.js` and `state.js`.
347	  - `view-model.js`.
348	  - `render/*.js`, plus `net/poll.js` and `main.js`.
349	- **One `Lease` type.**
350	  - It holds `key`, `binding`, `expires`, `deadline`, `closed` and `floor`.
351	  - `admit(candidate, now, rtt)` never renews the same key, closes on a scope boundary and keeps a sequence floor.
352	  - Lanes differ only through a declared `{ttlMs, scopeParts}` table.
353	- **One-way flow.**
354	  - `reduce(state, snapshot, now)` returns the new state plus a `health {healthy, reasons[]}` object.
355	  - `viewModel(state, now)` turns that into strings, tones and validity values.
356	  - Renderers patch the DOM only when their signature changes.
357	  - A dirty flag, coalesced with `requestAnimationFrame`, decides when to render.
358	  - A single timer is set for the earliest lease deadline.
359	- **One visual vocabulary for validity.** Current, provisional, last-read and unknown each get a shape, a colour, an opacity and a visible word. The same treatment applies to seats, pot and board, including under `forced-colors`.
360	- **Tests.**
361	  - Tests import modules directly instead of rewriting the source.
362	  - Pure reducer and lease tests do most of the work.
363	  - A thin real-browser layer checks visibility.
364	  - ESLint and `tsc --checkJs --noEmit` run as dev-only checks.

# coinpoker-help: Monitor frontend appraisal and full repository progress analysis

Date: 2026-10-15. Branch `checkpoint/seated-read-mechanism-2-20261002`, HEAD `5889f14` (2026-10-14) plus the uncommitted refactor in the worktree.

## 1. Executive summary

**What the project is.** coinpoker-help is a Windows proof of concept. It captures a CoinPoker table window, reads it with a locally fine-tuned 256M-parameter vision model (Laya, served on loopback port 18090), and turns the readings into leased, source-bound observations. A browser page, the Monitor, displays them. It also contains poker math and opponent-model crates that are meant to turn full observations into experimental advice.

**Where it stands.** The guard-rail engineering is unusually strong:
- leases that can only shorten;
- acceptance floors that can only rise;
- a SHA-256 witness on every field;
- hardened loopback HTTP;
- a locked, pinned toolchain.

That machinery also passes its own tests. On 2026-10-15, 623 Rust tests and 814 Python tests passed, and fmt and clippy were clean.

**Frontend verdict: 5.6/10.** The Monitor's core is trustworthy by construction. It never shows a number that has not been admitted. Its most important signals, though, do not reach the operator:
- After one failed poll, fields that were never read are labelled "Stale".
- The status word is permanently the success colour, even when it says "Disconnected".
- Whether a seat value is current, last-read or provisional is shown only by a 7 px dot or a text colour.
- The most useful empty-state message is hidden from sighted users.
- Yesterday's stopped session appears as the current state.

Under these sit a 2,858-line single-function `app.js` with nine hand-written lease state machines, and a 10 Hz full re-render.

**Repository verdict: about 60% of the HANDOFF Definition of Done, and about 25% of the original goal of live seated decision support.** The end-to-end path from capture to browser worked once:
- the 2026-10-12 run matched Pot and three stacks exactly over 191 s;
- that check was made by an agent, not a human.

It has not been reproduced on the current sustained path:
- In the latest sustained run, the dashboard consumer silently discarded 12 of 16 model readings. It judges freshness on its own lagging clock, and one stale heartbeat disqualifies a whole generation.
- In a recorded browser session, no field was ever shown as current.

**Hard limits.** The board read cannot pass its pinned 1.0 floor (0 of 330 units), and refitting it needs human labels first. No human has reviewed any label. The decision pipeline has never run on a real capture.

**Process risks.** These are acute:
- The refactor cannot be committed piecemeal.
- CI almost certainly fails Python collection on a clean runner.
- The test suite writes synthetic sessions into the private evidence tree.
- 93.5% of tracked bytes are generated graph output and a third-party PDF.
- GitHub's default branch still shows the retired macOS/Gemma product.

**Next step.** Commit the refactor as a unit, fix the consumer freshness veto, and re-run the Definition of Done on a build that the receipts record by hash.

## 2. Scorecard

| Area | Item | Score | One-line rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend | Information architecture and workflow | 5/10 | Rigorous validity logic, but no next step, hidden empty state, green status, false "Stale" |
| Frontend | Visual design and layout | 6/10 | Good palette and 800x600 fit; colour-only validity, 375 px overlap, unused width at 1280 px |
| Frontend | Accessibility | 6/10 | Correct tablist, focus and live region; validity colour-only, 10 Hz list rebuilds, Start/Stop drop focus |
| Frontend | Front-end engineering | 4/10 | Fail-closed and well tested, inside an untooled 2,858-line IIFE |
| Frontend | Security and robustness | 7/10 | Strict CSP and Host/Origin checks verified live; DTO contradicts SECURITY.md |
| Frontend | Runtime performance | 5/10 | Bounded, but about 14 renders/s and a new TCP connection every 250 ms while idle |
| Frontend | Contract and test fidelity | 6/10 | Lease semantics faithful; five documented UI promises contradicted |
| **Frontend** | **Overall** | **5.6/10** | **Trustworthy core; operator-facing signals broken** |
| Repository | Architecture and code quality | C+ (64) | Clean seams and a verified Rust/Python geometry twin; much dead code, four geometry frames |
| Repository | Readiness against the Definition of Done | C- (52) | Worked once; the sustained path loses three quarters of its readings |
| Repository | Verification integrity | C- (57) | Large, honest, fully synthetic test estate; CI likely red; stale docs |
| Repository | Security, privacy, licensing | B- (71) | Strong loopback hardening; privacy claims contradicted by shipped code |
| Repository | Process and hygiene | D+ (42) | Excellent toolchain pinning; mega-commits, bloat, diverged default branch |
| Repository | Delivery trajectory | C+ (62) | Fast, evidence-driven pivots; demonstration not repeated |
| Repository | Risk posture | D+ (40) | Top risks have no owner and are mostly self-inflicted |

input.title: Fix dashboard freshness veto dropping readings
input.name: freshness-veto-fix
input.prompt:
Fix the consumer-side freshness veto in scripts/laya_dashboard.py that silently drops model-path partial_observation readings, and pin it with tests.

The defect, verified in code:
- Around line 1072-1073, DashboardState marks a capture_health heartbeat fresh only if `now - captured < 1000`, where `now` is the consumer's clock. The supervisor lags 0.5-1.3 s behind the producer during sustained runs, so heartbeats that the producer marked fresh become non-fresh here.
- A non-fresh heartbeat calls `_invalidate("capture-not-fresh")` (around line 1093). `_invalidate` raises `invalidated_version` to the current (gen, epoch) (around lines 762-764), and that version is only cleared at stream start or reset.
- The partial_observation branch (around lines 1139-1149) then rejects any partial whose (gen, epoch) is at or below `invalidated_version`. It returns before the ledger write, so the drop leaves only a sequence gap.

In private run d643, this explains all 12 of the 16 dropped partials: every dropped one followed a non-fresh heartbeat of the same generation, and none of the 4 admitted ones did.

Required changes:
1. Judge freshness at the producer's emit time (`emitted - captured < 1000`). Keep the existing delivery-delay bound (the `now - emitted >= HEARTBEAT_MS` check near line 1059).
2. A non-fresh heartbeat must not permanently poison its generation. Either do not raise `invalidated_version` for capture-not-fresh, or clear it when a later fresh heartbeat of the same (gen, epoch) arrives. Keep lease non-renewal intact: deadlines may only shorten.
3. Write a ledger row with an explicit reason before every partial-observation rejection return.
4. Add tests:
   - a heartbeat delivered 1,000-2,499 ms after capture but emitted promptly stays fresh, and a following partial is admitted;
   - a non-fresh then fresh heartbeat in the same generation still admits the partial;
   - every rejection writes a ledger reason.
   The current helper in scripts/tests/test_laya_dashboard_stage2.py sets emitted = captured = now, which is why no test caught this.

Done when the full Python suite passes with the pinned runtime and the new tests fail on the old code. Run the suite with the main checkout's interpreter: C:/Users/cld-main/Desktop/github-projects/coinpoker-help/.local/laya-runtime/env/python.exe -B -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests. Do not start the server, load the model, capture windows, or touch the poker client. Do not commit; report the diff.

**Frontend: 5.6/10.** The Monitor never shows a number it hasn't validated, and its loopback hardening passed my live probes. Its most important signals don't reach you:
- **False "Stale" labels.** After one failed poll, fields that were never read are labelled "Stale". I reproduced this live.

- **Hidden message.** The clearest empty-state message is visible only to screen readers.
- **Old session shown as current.** Yesterday's stopped session appears as the current state, with no date.
- **Hard to maintain.** All of it lives in one 2,858-line function that re-renders the whole page ten times a second.

**Repository: about 60% of the handoff's Definition of Done, and about 25% of the original goal of live seated advice.** The capture-to-browser path worked once, on 2026-10-12, and it hasn't been reproduced since.
- **Why readings are lost.** In the latest sustained run, the dashboard silently discarded 12 of 16 model readings. It judges freshness on its own lagging clock, and one stale heartbeat disqualifies a whole generation. Model latency was not the cause.
- **Board reads are blocked.** They cannot pass the pinned 1.0 confidence floor, and refitting it needs human-reviewed labels first. No human has reviewed any label yet.
- **Process risks:**

  - The test suite writes synthetic sessions into your private evidence folder.

- To start it, I added an untracked file, `.claude/launch.json`.
- My test run added 114 synthetic session folders under `.local/laya/train/`, because that is how the test suite currently behaves.
